title: Confluence and Management
lessons/price-action-u3-l1/steps/0/body: **Confluence** means several **independent** reasons lining up at one spot: say, an uptrend + key support + a bullish pin bar + a round number. Each factor nudges the odds up a little, but no combination gives you **certainty**.
lessons/price-action-u3-l1/steps/1/body: Before you enter, ask yourself: Is the **trend** on my side? Am I at a **key level**? Do I have a clear price **signal**? Is the **risk-to-reward** at least 1:2? Every "no" makes the setup weaker.
lessons/price-action-u3-l1/steps/2/promp: Which setup has the most confluence?
lessons/price-action-u3-l1/steps/2/optio: A bullish pin bar on support, in an uptrend
A bullish pin bar mid-range, far from any level
A counter-trend inside bar in the middle of the chart
A plain green candle after a news release
lessons/price-action-u3-l1/steps/2/expla: The first option has three independent factors: trend, level and signal. The others have one at most.
lessons/price-action-u3-l1/steps/3/promp: Which combination of factors do you see on this chart?
lessons/price-action-u3-l1/steps/3/optio: Uptrend + support on a round number + bullish pin bar
Just a bullish candle with no level
lessons/price-action-u3-l1/steps/3/expla: In an uptrend, price broke 1.1000 and has now formed a bullish pin bar right on that level (a round number too). Three independent factors together.
lessons/price-action-u3-l1/steps/4/state: The more confluence factors you have, the more certain the trade is to win.
lessons/price-action-u3-l1/steps/4/expla: Confluence only raises the odds; even the best setups lose sometimes. That's why you always need a stop loss and risk management.
lessons/price-action-u3-l1/steps/5/body: Three momentum indicators all saying the same thing aren't **three reasons**; they're one reason repeated three times. Real confluence combines **different kinds** of evidence: structure, level, candle signal and timing.
lessons/price-action-u3-l1/steps/6/promp: There are two bullish pin bars on this chart. Tap the one with more confluence.
lessons/price-action-u3-l1/steps/6/expla: The second pin bar formed right on support and price bounced from it. The first one was mid-move with no level behind it.
lessons/price-action-u3-l1/steps/7/promp: The trend is down, price rallied back to resistance at 2430 and formed a bearish pin bar. What's your call?
lessons/price-action-u3-l1/steps/7/expla: The downtrend, key resistance and a bearish pin bar all point the same way. Continuation down is more likely. Stop loss just above the pin bar's wick.
lessons/price-action-u3-l2/steps/0/body: Trade management starts **before you enter**: write down your stop loss, take profit and rules for moving them. The most important rule: **never move your stop loss further away**. You can only move it closer, in the trade's favor.
lessons/price-action-u3-l2/steps/1/body: Two common methods: once price moves **1R** in your favor, move your stop loss to **your entry (breakeven)**. Or, in a trend, move your stop loss **below each new higher low (HL)**. That's called a **trailing stop**.
lessons/price-action-u3-l2/steps/1/visua: Stop loss below the last HL
lessons/price-action-u3-l2/steps/2/promp: Which of these is a common trade management mistake?
lessons/price-action-u3-l2/steps/2/optio: Moving your stop loss further away as price gets close
Moving your stop loss to entry after 1R
Closing part of the trade at the first target
Writing your exit plan before you enter
lessons/price-action-u3-l2/steps/2/expla: Widening your stop loss means taking more risk than you planned, turning a small loss into a big one. The other options are sound management.
lessons/price-action-u3-l2/steps/3/state: Moving your stop loss to entry after a 1R move takes that trade's risk to almost zero.
lessons/price-action-u3-l2/steps/3/expla: If price turns back, the trade closes around breakeven; only slippage or a gap might cost a little. Of course, you're also more likely to get stopped out early.
lessons/price-action-u3-l2/steps/4/promp: You're long and trailing your stop loss below the higher lows. Tap the candle that made the latest higher low (HL).
lessons/price-action-u3-l2/steps/4/expla: After the previous high, this candle hit the lowest point of the pullback, and then price made a new high. It's the latest HL, and your trailing stop goes just below it.
lessons/price-action-u3-l2/steps/5/body: Many traders close part of the trade at the **first target** (like 1R or 2R) and hold the rest with a trailing stop. It locks in profit and eases the mental pressure, but it also shrinks your **maximum possible profit**.
lessons/price-action-u3-l2/steps/6/promp: Long EUR/USD with 1R = 30 pips. At 1R you close half and move the rest's stop loss to entry. Then price turns back and hits the new stop. What's the result for the whole trade?
lessons/price-action-u3-l2/steps/6/expla: The first half closed at 1R profit, which is +0.5R for the whole trade. The second half closed at breakeven (0). Total: +0.5R.
lessons/price-action-u3-l2/steps/7/promp: Put the steps of managing a trade in order.
lessons/price-action-u3-l2/steps/7/items: Set stop loss and take profit before entry
Enter with a size that fits your risk
Price reaches 1R, close part of the position
Trail your stop loss below new lows
Exit at take profit or the trailing stop
lessons/price-action-u3-l2/steps/7/expla: A plan before entry, size based on risk, then lock in some profit, and finally let the rest of the trade ride the trend.
lessons/price-action-u3-l2/steps/8/sente: Many traders move their stop loss to their ___ point once the trade's profit reaches ___.
lessons/price-action-u3-l2/steps/8/expla: After a 1R move, moving your stop loss to entry makes the trade almost risk-free.
lessons/price-action-u3-l3/steps/0/body: Log every trade in a **journal**: setup type, reason for entry, entry, stop loss and take profit, result in **R**, and a before-and-after **screenshot**. Without a log, you'll never know which setup really works for you.
lessons/price-action-u3-l3/steps/1/body: After enough trades (say a few dozen per setup), work out the **expectancy**: (win rate × average win) − (loss rate × average loss). If it's positive, the setup has an edge in the long run.
lessons/price-action-u3-l3/steps/1/tip: A low win rate with big wins can still be profitable. What matters is expectancy.
lessons/price-action-u3-l3/steps/2/promp: Your pin bar setup wins 50% of the time with an average win of 1.5R, and loses 50% with an average loss of 1R. What's the expectancy per trade?
lessons/price-action-u3-l3/steps/3/pairs: Pin bar, inside bar, false break…
Profit or loss relative to initial risk
A picture of the chart before and after the trade
Fear, greed or rushing at entry
lessons/price-action-u3-l3/steps/4/state: 10 trades are enough to judge confidently whether a setup is profitable.
lessons/price-action-u3-l3/steps/4/expla: The result of 10 trades is mostly luck. For a reliable picture, you need a much bigger sample.
lessons/price-action-u3-l3/steps/5/body: Once a week, go over your trades and **tag your mistakes**: early entries, moved stop losses, off-plan trades. Look for patterns: which setup and which market work best? Change **only one thing** at a time.
lessons/price-action-u3-l3/steps/6/promp: You're reviewing a winning trade. Tap the candle that was the setup's main signal (a pin bar on support).
lessons/price-action-u3-l3/steps/6/expla: This candle dipped below 60,000 and closed above support with a long lower wick: a bullish pin bar on support, and the trend turned after it. That's what you log in your journal with a screenshot.
lessons/price-action-u3-l3/steps/7/promp: After 60 trades, your journal shows pin bars at key levels have an expectancy of +0.5R and inside bars mid-range −0.3R. What's the most sensible decision?
lessons/price-action-u3-l3/steps/7/optio: Focus on pin bars at levels and drop inside bars in ranges
Double your inside bar size to win back the losses
Ditch the journal because the results differ
Swap your whole system for a brand-new method
lessons/price-action-u3-l3/steps/7/expla: That's exactly what a journal is for: keep the setup with a positive edge, and drop or fix the one with negative expectancy.
lessons/price-action-u3-l3/steps/8/promp: Put the setup review cycle in order.
lessons/price-action-u3-l3/steps/8/items: Log the setup, reason for entry and a screenshot
Log the trade's result in R
Work out win rate and expectancy
lessons/price-action-u3-l3/steps/8/expla: First you collect data, then you group and calculate, and finally you decide based on numbers, not feelings.
